ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: personal stories
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: A few times a year, one colonist's own story, in three to five stages over days to a season; some are stories of three.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: Read the journals now and then. That's where most of these get told.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description:
A few times a year, one colonist's own story begins: a journey home, a quarrel mended, an apprenticeship that ends in a fine piece of work, a grief that slowly eases. Each grows out of what Rimfolk already knows about that colonist (their losses, rivals, secrets, life goals, feelings, skills, animals and the council's dealings with them), never from a roll alone, and moves on through three to five stages over days to a season as things happen in play. Some are stories of three: two rivals for one person's affection, a teacher with two students, a parent and two children at odds, a friend caught between two friends. A colonist has at most one story at a time.
The Story tab shows where a colonist's story stands, what it waits for next and how close it is, and the stories they've lived through.

li.heading: How a story moves
li.text:
Each stage waits for something to happen: days to pass, a skill level reached, hours of work at a skill, a conversation between the two people in it (it shows in the social log), something made of good enough quality, a fight at home come through on their feet, a bond with an animal, another dream, a wish granted, a life goal reached, or a stretch of days with something holding (a good mood, a room of their own, getting along). Each hour it holds counts; each hour it doesn't takes half an hour back, so a bad evening costs a little and a bad week costs the lot.
Every stage writes a line in the colonist's journal in their own voice (a kind colonist and an abrasive one tell it differently), often one in the other person's journal too, and a line in the chronicle. When a story ends well, a letter retells it from the start. While a colonist is away on a journey, their story waits, and so does its clock.
What happens around them can move a waiting story on too (with "Systems talk to each other" on): a calendar day kept counts as a day, and as the word they were waiting to have with someone who kept it with them; a people repaying an old good turn, a friend made at a camp, or getting back to full strength after convalescing move it on a day or two. Colonists whose work keeps going wrong, whom the council keeps letting down, or who keep missing the colony's company are twice as likely to begin the story that answers it.

table.li: Story | Begins when | Moves on through | Can leave behind

The long way home | Someone has been away 5 days or more, with a person they love waiting at home | Coming home; a talk about the road | A friendship, a name (the Wanderer, after 15 days away), a quirk
Somewhere to belong | A newcomer (2 to 25 days here) is homesick, lonely or short of belonging | A welcome from an old hand; a room of their own; good days | Trust in the council
A companion | An animal lover, or a kind or lonely colonist, is master of an animal with no bond | Hours together; time spent handling; trust | A bond with the animal
Grudging respect | Rivals share a passion, or fought side by side | Hours working near each other; a word of respect; days of getting along | The rivalry ended, a friendship
Old wounds | Former lovers, family at odds, or a friend who let a secret slip | Quiet days without a sharp word; a talk; days of getting along | The quarrel ended, a friendship, strain lifted
An old debt | Someone rescued, tended, covered for or spoke up for them | Days; hours of work on a gift; giving it | A friendship
Second chances | Their trust in the council is doubtful or bitter | One of their wishes granted; days of trusting it more | Trust

The apprentice's masterwork | A keen crafter, artist or builder (level 4 to 11) has a master (12 or better) to learn from | 2 levels gained; the master's eye; something excellent made | An inspiration, a name (Steadyhand), a quirk, rarely a deeper passion
A calling | A child or a teenager, and a grown-up good at something (8 or better) | Questions; practice; a level gained | A friendship, rarely a new passion
Passing it on | An elder (55 or older) or an old hand (3 years here) with a skill of 12 or better | An offer to teach; the student gains 2 levels; the last lessons | A mentorship, lessons
A long grief | Someone close died in the last few weeks | Days; talking about them or dreaming of them; better days | Strain lifted, a quirk
A secret told | Someone with a secret has a close friend | Days; confiding in the friend; steady days; telling everyone | The secret out, strain lifted

A fear faced | An enemy who hurt them got away, or they dread the dark, storms or the eclipse | Days; training; a fight at home come through, or the enemy gone for good (going for that very enemy in a fight ends it at once) | The dread gone, strain lifted, a name (the Unafraid)

The fear laid to rest | The enemy who hurt them is in the colony's cells, or gone for good in the last 40 days (dead, let go, one of ours, vanished), and they're still afraid, haunted lately or sleeping badly | Days to take it in; telling a friend the whole of it; good days and quiet nights, or the prisoner's fate settled (going for that very enemy in a fight, say a prisoner breaking out, ends it at once, as for a fear faced) | Strain lifted, a lighter heart for days
The recurring dream | The same strange dream 2 or more times in 12 days | Another dream; telling someone; making something of it | Strain lifted, sometimes an inspiration
A grudge laid down | A vendetta 15 days old or more, and someone tired of carrying it | Days; talking it over; calmer days | The vendetta laid down, strain lifted
Within reach | Halfway or more to a life goal, 10 days or more in | A push from a friend; the goal reached | A friend's good opinion

A rival in love | Two colonists, neither attached, are both fond of the same unattached person | Time together; a word between the rivals; the choice, a romance or, after weeks, how the one they're fond of feels | Love for one, a setback for the other, sometimes respect between the rivals

Torn between two students | A teacher with two mentorships in one craft, or two keen learners of what they do best | A fair word for each; the two making up between themselves; both coming on | Two mentorships, the students friends

Brothers and sisters | A parent with two children at home (Biotech's children or grown) at odds with each other | A quiet word with each; days without a sharp word between them; thinking better of each other | The two friends again, strain lifted
Caught in the middle | Two of their friends have fallen out (at odds, rivals or a sharp word lately) | A talk with each; the two talking it out, or getting on | The two friends again, strain lifted
The road calls | A camp on the land whose fire they've sat at, and a restless heart | A talk about the road; the camp packing up and going | They stay; strain lifted, a friend, sometimes a quirk
The weight of office | Seated on the council at the last election, 12 days ago or less | Advice from the speaker or a friend; steady days; a hard call | Trust, a little practice in talking

Word from far away | Hard times out in the world (plague, famine, war, flood...) and family of theirs out there in it | Sharing the worry; the trouble ending | Relief, or, if the relative dies first, a real loss

Bad nights (Biotech) | A child with nightmares or a fright that won't let go, and a parent or fond grown-up | Sitting up with them; good days or a better dream | Rest, a friendship, sometimes a light by the bed

Not a child any more | A young person (13 to 19) at odds with a parent or an older colonist | Hard work at what they love; a talk as equals; days of getting on | Trust, a friendship, the rivalry ended, rarely a passion
A new parent (Biotech) | A baby of theirs born in the last few days | Days; a pair of hands from someone; good days | Rest, a friendship, strain lifted

One more spring | Someone 65 or older whose body has begun to fail (a lasting condition or poor health) | Telling someone their wishes; one last piece of work; good days | A small mood, strain lifted, sometimes stories for the little ones
The last two of us | Two colonists of 55 or more, long at odds | Hours near each other; the old days remembered; getting on | Friends at last, strain lifted

The long discipline (A RimWorld of Magic) | A mage or a fighter has someone 5 class levels further along in the same art, or is frustrated with themselves and has a close friend | A talk about the art; a class level gained; a few quiet days | Strain lifted, a friendship

li.heading: Stories of three
li.text: In a story of three, a stage can wait on the colonist and the third person, or on the other two between themselves: two students making up, two brothers at peace, two friends talking again. What passes between two of the three at the end (a memory of each other, a bond) waits until those two are really together, and after a few hours one of them goes to find the other. If the third dies or leaves, the story ends there. A rival in love ends one of three ways: chosen, not chosen (a real setback, for a week or so), or neither, when the rivals often end up respecting each other.

li.heading: Endings, good and otherwise
li.text:
The good moods come at the end, not along the way, and they're modest: Rimfolk memories, sharing the budget of good moods with everything else Rimfolk gives. Most of the newer endings give something other than mood: a feeling, rest, trust, a little practice. Some stories leave something lasting: a friendship, a mentorship, a rivalry ended, trust in the council, strain lifted, an inspiration, a quirk (tells stories of the road, marks every piece, sets a place for the lost, sleeps with a light burning, tells the little ones stories) or a name the colony gives (the Wanderer, Steadyhand, the Unafraid). Very rarely a calling or a masterwork deepens a passion.
A story can also fizzle: a stage that waits too long, a fight that reopens the quarrel, a secret that comes out before it could be told, the enemy's banners at the walls again. That gets a journal line and a chronicle line too, and sometimes a real setback: children still at odds, a friend still caught in the middle, a seat on the council lost too soon, a young one still treated like a child, family dead far away. If the other person in it dies or leaves, the story ends there (unless they were only a friend to talk to). If the colonist dies before it ends, the chronicle says so, and a day later the other person in it, or whoever was closest, writes about what was left unfinished.

li.heading: How often
li.text: Set it under Options, Mod options, Rimfolk, People & moods: off, rare (about 2 a year in a colony of 6), normal (about 4) or frequent (about 7). One to three colonists see three quarters as many, and from 12 up to half again as many. One story runs at a time on rare, 2 on normal and 3 on frequent, one more from 9 colonists. Off: none begin, and any under way wait where they are.

li.heading: On the map
li.text: With "Answers play out on the map" on, a story's stages happen where you can see them. The one home from the long way sits up by the fire telling the road, a grief that has eased takes its colonist to sit by the grave, the gift that settles an old debt is carried over by hand and set down at the other's feet, and the old crafter passing it on hands the student their old knife the same way. A secret told is said in front of whoever gathers to hear it: the colony is called together, and it comes out at the end. The recurring dream ends with a long look at the thing that was made of it. A companion animal that has taken to following its master keeps at their heels for a day and a half (danger, drafting or the master leaving the map ends it). Rivals shake hands, the last two of a generation sit on the bench in the sun, and a grown-up sits up by a child's bed after bad nights. If it can't happen, the story goes on all the same.
